subject: Scale pathways post-call: FastPay SLO & burst readiness
messages:
From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@fastpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Bowers <alex.bowers@fastpay.com>, FastPay SRE <sre@fastpay.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + perf targets (post-call)

Thanks for the call earlier — good to meet the team. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying numbers so your engineers can size things: 

- Traffic profile: traffic is spiky; mean QPS during business hours ~450, peak bursts up to ~3,000 for ~2–5 minute windows.
- Typical request: text-generation API, median token length ~120, 95th ~450.
- Latency/SLOs we care about: p95 end-to-end <= 350 ms, p99 <= 950 ms for non-streaming; for streaming we need first-byte (time-to-first-chunk) <= 200 ms and steady-chunk latency under 100 ms.
- Concurrency expectation: baseline concurrency ~200 active connections; concurrency must scale to ~1,200 during peak bursts.
- Streaming: we use chunked responses for progressive rendering in the UI; client keeps a single connection per session for up to 60s.
- Durability/ordering: KV cache warmup matters — cold-cache responses add ~50–150 ms.

Next steps from our side: provide a small sample of production traces (anonymized) and the attached spreadsheet with a week of minute-level QPS and token distribution. We can run a joint load test in the next 2 weeks if you can give a suggested window.

Thanks — Nora
Nora Chen
Head of Product, FastPay
---
Attachments: fastpay-qps-sample.csv (referenced, uploaded separately)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Nora Chen <nora.chen@fastpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 17:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf targets (post-call)

Nora — thanks for the clear recap and the spreadsheet. Really helpful. Below is a short post-call mutual action plan and a set of asks so Karthik and the infra team can size the warm pool & autoscale behavior properly.

Mutual action plan (high level):
1) Redwood to review FastPay traces + sample QPS file (we have it).
2) Redwood infra deep-dive: propose warm-pool sizing, queue/backpressure strategy, and a failover path (model variant or region) by EOD Tue (2025-05-20).
3) Joint load test: target window 2025-05-27 02:00–04:00 PT (please confirm).
4) Post-test: capture p50/p95/p99, time-to-first-chunk for streaming, and cold/warm cache delta; iterate on warm-pool sizing.

Asks / inputs we need now:
- Confirm whether the 3,000 QPS peaks are sustained on the minute boundary or if they're sub-minute spikes (helps with queueing model).
- Send an anonymized sample of the longest streaming sessions (IDs are fine).
- Any constraints on using a cross-region fallback during bursts?

Initial sizing notes (ballpark) — for planning only:
- Warm pool: we will propose keeping a prewarmed pool able to serve ~600 concurrent streaming sessions to hit the first-byte SLO for most bursts; additional on-demand capacity will be used to reach 1.2k.
- Scale-up delta: small-scale boosts (<=200 extra sessions) expected to spin up in ~6–12s depending on packing; large fills (hundreds of GPUs) will use staged ramping + queueing with target 30–45s to achieve usable throughput.
- Queueing policy: short tail-priority (95% fast-path), with a bounded request queue and guaranteed fallback to a lower-cost model variant when latency is at risk.

I attached a draft "burst-slo-matrix.xlsx" (simple matrix mapping burst size -> warm pool -> expected p95/p99). Karthik — can you review and convert this into an action-ready sizing doc? Monica — I'll follow up on contracting/credits conversation after we lock technicals.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0133

Attachments: burst-slo-matrix.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 19:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf targets (post-call) — infra notes

Internal notes / technical follow-ups for the sizing doc: 

1) Warm-pool sizing approach:
- We should size prewarmed instances by peak-first-byte budget rather than concurrent sessions alone. Given FastPay's median tokens and streaming behavior, estimate each prewarmed unit handles ~8–12 active streaming sessions hitting first-byte SLO simultaneously (depends on model flops & sequence length).
- Recommend initial warm pool to target ~600 sessions -> translate to ~60–80 prewarmed units (we'll map to instance shapes after we see model selection).

2) Scale-up timing & phases:
- Phase 0 (fast-path): use warm pool for first 60s of a burst to keep TTFB low.
- Phase 1 (rapid scale): autoscaler allocates additional preemptible/ephemeral capacity; expect 6–20s to start accepting traffic per new worker (includes container start + model load/kv warm).
- Phase 2 (steady-state): after ~30–45s additional capacity will be fully warmed via prefix caching and KV seeding; p99 should converge to within ~10–20% of warm-path.

3) Queueing and backpressure:
- Suggest a boundedMPSC queue per route with a short time-to-live (TTL) ~= 6s. If queue fills, move traffic to degraded path (smaller model or partial response) rather than dropping.
- For streaming connections, keep connection open and stream partial tokens if full inference is delayed; this preserves client UX.

4) Observability & test metrics:
- We need per-request traces with these fields: request_id, arrival_ts, first_byte_ts, final_byte_ts, model_variant, worker_id, cache_hit(boolean), tokens_in, tokens_out.
- Karthik to own the runbook draft and the load-test playbook; target to share by Mon (2025-05-19).

I'll draft a warm-pool-diagram.pdf that maps phases above and the fallback decision tree.

-karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@fastpay.com>

Sean / Karthik — thanks, this all looks sensible. A few replies inline: 

- Peaks: the 3k spikes are usually 2–3 minute sustained windows, not just instantaneous bursts.
- Cross-region fallback: allowed as long as data residency is respected for EU customers (not applicable to our primary region here).
- We can confirm the joint test window 2025-05-27 02:00–04:00 PT. We'll invite Engineering & SRE and will attach anonymized streaming traces and the QPS spreadsheet to the Drive folder (shared link below).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FastPay-Scale-Prep
Doc: We uploaded a 1-week minute-level CSV and a sample of 50 streaming traces.

Please proceed with the sizing doc and runbook; if you can get the warm-pool diagram and the initial runbook by Tue (2025-05-20) that works for our team.

Nora
